chapter_title: Chương 19: Đánh bài không nhất thiết phải có tứ quý thủ công

segments.title: Chương 19: Đánh bài không nhất thiết phải có tứ quý thủ công
segments.content:
The pay-to-win systems of later generations were like a royal flush in this era.

But could you not play cards just because you didn't have a royal flush?

He didn't need to lead the market by too much, just a slight lead would be enough to stand out among the various private servers.

Chen Guiliang decided to research the market first. He immediately asked, "Cousin-uncle, what kind of Legend private servers are popular right now? I mean, compared to the official servers, how insane are the leveling speed and equipment?"

Feng Tao said, "Most of them just slightly increase the leveling speed and equipment drop rates. As for equipment, the most popular new trend is to port things over from The Legend of Mir 3."

In later years, there were five types of Legend private servers: Shanda-emulation, Lightly-Modified, Micro-Modified, Mid-Modified, and Super-Modified.

Players from different eras liked different types.

According to his cousin-uncle, Shanda-emulation, Lightly-Modified, and Micro-Modified were the popular ones now.

He couldn't just rely on hearsay; he had to experience it for himself.

"Cousin-uncle, I want to play a Legend private server. Which one is the most popular right now?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Private server versions changed quickly, and Feng Tao wasn't sure either.

He had Chen Guiliang move aside, sat down at the computer himself, and quickly opened a forum, saying, "This is the 7GG forum. It didn't deal with private servers at first, but now it's the biggest private server hub in the country."

"But they don't have the best tech. The experts on the Ledo forum are especially amazing. The 17577 forum is the favorite among newbies. A complete newbie who knows nothing can set up a private server version they provide after just two or three hours of learning."

"My favorite expert is called 'noyeys.' The new features and technologies he develops are often shared selflessly..."

Feng Tao spoke with familiarity, commenting on the major forums and tech experts.

Seeing how enthusiastic he was, Chen Guiliang didn't have the heart to interrupt. He could only chime in and shoot the breeze with his cousin-uncle, taking note of the names of those forums and experts.

Feng Tao selected a popular private server and, while downloading it, continued to ramble on. He spoke eloquently for half an hour until his cousin-aunt's voice came from outside the study: "Time for bed!"

"Coming, coming."

Feng Tao dropped the mouse and said to Chen Guiliang, "You play by yourself. I'm going to bed."

The private server was almost finished downloading, but Chen Guiliang's attention had shifted to those forums.

He carefully browsed through the various hot threads, studying the current private server players, and recorded his summaries on A4 paper.

The main contents of the hot threads were summarized as follows:

First, complaining about the official Shanda servers, saying the new maps were boring and became tasteless after a few days, not worth wasting game time cards on.

Second, cursing The World of Legend as trash.

Third, complaining that current private servers lacked creativity, that the thousands of them were all largely the same, and that the server administrators only knew how to make money.

Fourth, complaining that private servers introducing new features had too many bugs.

Fifth, praising the experts who selflessly shared their technology and cursing those who hoarded their tech to sell for money.

After the first private server finished downloading, Chen Guiliang started downloading a second popular one.

He registered and logged into the first one, quickly entering the game.

He found that the leveling speed was ridiculously slow, probably only two or three times faster than the official Legend server.

After leveling up a few times, Chen Guiliang stopped grinding mobs and instead ran to the major safe zones to check the equipment of the top players.

Based on the content of the public chat, he could basically conclude that this private server made money by selling the six major heavyweight armors, along with weapons like the Wrath Blade, Dragon Tooth, and逍遥扇 (Boundless Fan).

There were even free-to-play players unwilling to spend money, using female characters played by men to desperately look for a "husband" in the public chat, just begging a rich player to gift "her" a Boundless Fan.

Chen Guiliang smiled and wrote on the A4 paper: Popularize all equipment from before the heavyweight armor version. Everyone can afford a Demon-God Armor; everyone can afford a Dragon Tooth and Wrath Blade. Spiritual poverty alleviation.

After uninstalling this private server, Chen Guiliang installed the second one.

The second one was quite interesting. Its selling point was porting equipment from The Legend of Mir 3. It also ported textures from The Legend of Mir 3 for partial beautification of the private server. But it couldn't achieve a complete overhaul, so it looked quite awkward at first glance, creating a stitched-together chimera.

The leveling speed was also very slow, perhaps four or five times that of the official Legend server.

Chen Guiliang wrote on the A4 paper: Leveling speed can be increased by more than twenty times compared to the official version. The Legend of Mir 3's top equipment can be modified with overpowered stats. Make money by selling overpowered equipment.

The basic approach for making a private server was set: create a super-overpowered version of Legend to broaden the horizons of the current naive players!

Chen Guiliang turned off the computer and sat at the desk, thinking for a long time.

If he were to collaborate with someone on a private server with nothing but empty words, even if his partner didn't burn the bridge after crossing it, he probably wouldn't get much of the profit.

He had to find a way to get something for nothing, to secure a sum of money first!

Of course, if he couldn't get it, so be it. Every little bit he earned would be a gain, since he had neither the skills nor the capital.

After carefully going over the entire plan, Chen Guiliang began to write at his desk.

He wrote late into the night before going to bed.

The next day, early morning.

Feng Tao came into the study to get his satchel and saw a stack of A4 paper filled with writing on the computer desk.

He glanced at two pages out of curiosity, then lost interest and put it back.

"Guiliang, get up for breakfast!"

Lin Chunhong called out from the living room.

A short while later, the three of them were sitting around the table for breakfast.

Feng Tao asked casually, "Are you writing a game design document?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Not that detailed, just some game concepts and ideas. I plan to sell them to that Boss Tao."

Feng Tao thought this was a high school student's fantasy and teased, "He just runs an internet cafe, he doesn't make games himself. Why would he buy this stuff from you?"

Chen Guiliang didn't reveal his true intentions, saying half-truthfully, "It would be great if Boss Tao is interested. If not, I don't lose anything. Just trying my luck."

Feng Tao said, "I saw the title is 'Free-to-Play Games and Their Business Model.' If the game is free, how can it make money?"

Chen Guiliang smiled, "Aren't Legend private servers a type of free-to-play game?"

Feng Tao retorted, "That's different. Private servers can make a bit of money on the sly because of their low costs. If you were to develop or license a free-to-play game, you probably wouldn't even recover the costs."

"Haha." Chen Guiliang couldn't explain.

Before ZT Online became a massive hit, no one believed free-to-play games could make money.

Perhaps some people believed it, but the bigger the company, the more afraid they were to take the risk.

There was no point in being secretive.

Ideas like this expire and become worthless over time. Cashing in on them quickly for a small sum was a win in itself—in just another two or three years, most of the ideas on that A4 paper would be implemented by Shi Yuzhu.

Chen Guiliang was broke right now. If he waited until he earned his first pot of gold and then used his pay-to-win concepts to make a game himself, he wouldn't have enough time.

ZT Online would definitely beat him to it!

So, he might as well throw it out there and see.

If it really didn't work out, he could use his trip to Shanghai for the New Concept Composition Competition finals to peddle his ideas to a few big companies.

Although it was very likely to fail, what if it succeeded?

In any case, it was a no-cost venture, and he could cast a wide net and sell to multiple buyers.

As for the business talk today, that pay-to-win concept was just Chen Guiliang's way of testing the waters.

Otherwise, was he really going to con a small-time boss in a third-tier city into developing a game?

The difficulty of that would probably be no less than selling Melatonin to Shi Yuzhu.

"What are you guys talking about?" Lin Chunhong asked curiously.

Feng Tao smiled, "Guiliang wrote up a set of game concepts that can be used to develop an online game. He plans to sell it to Gang Ge today."

Lin Chunhong said, "Isn't making games very expensive? Does Boss Tao have that much money?"

"It's not about whether Gang Ge has enough money," Feng Tao explained in detail. "All your assets combined are only a few million. A high school student comes to you with a few pieces of paper and says you can make big money if you make a game according to this. Would you be willing to buy those papers, then sell your house and car and risk your entire fortune to make a game?"

"Impossible." Lin Chunhong shook her head repeatedly.

Then, she added, "Even if I were to make a game, I wouldn't buy those papers. It's all just written on paper anyway, I could just memorize it."

Chen Guiliang smiled.

In his eyes, the only question was whether to make the game or not. There was no way they could make the game and not pay him.

If the other party really dared to do that, it was still uncertain who would be screwing over whom.

At worst, he would just post the contents of the A4 paper on game forums and then print out dozens of copies to send to major game companies.

Some big company would eventually see its value and develop a similar game ahead of time.

In that scenario, Chen Guiliang would just miss out on the money, while the one who stiffed him might have invested millions and lost everything!

Mutually assured destruction.

One gets a scratch, the other gets his head chopped off.

Chen Guiliang was no goody-two-shoes.

—

[Regarding the 2002 leak of the Italian Legend server, the articles, posts, and videos circulating online, especially the more general ones, all insist it was a "source code leak."]

[But the real informative posts that involve specific people, sites, and technical details say it was the "server program" (including configuration files and scripts) that was leaked. There are also a few people who ran private servers back then who stated clearly that the complete Legend source code had never been leaked before the Lingfeng Studio disbanded.]

I hate people who only tell half the story!

Someone who could treat Yue Guan as their "white moonlight" girl, how could they be...
